slides.headline: She'd lost her first Super Series final the year before. This time, she didn't let it slip.
On November 20, 2016, PV Sindhu beat China's Sun Yu to win the China Open, her first Super Series Premier title.
slides.body: Sindhu won 21-11, 17-21, 21-11 in Fuzhou - the top tier of the BWF Super Series circuit at the time, and a bigger title than the Denmark Open final she'd lost the year before.

slides.headline: It was proof she could finish what her near-misses had started.
slides.body: Sindhu had already won Olympic silver at Rio 2016 just months earlier. The China Open title showed that result wasn't a one-off - it was the start of a run that would eventually include a World Championship gold.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat keeps producing athletes who turn a near-miss into the next title.
slides.body: Sindhu's China Open win is one data point in a longer pattern - Indian badminton's rise from occasional upsets to a program that expects to win at the top level.
